details: a streaming client read of a gzip response gave the whole received chunk to the decoder at once, so about 1 MB of hostile gzip could ask for up to 1 GiB of output in one step (6.4 GB of memory in 0.51.0 for a 1000 MB bomb, now 23 MB); the body now goes to the decoder 4 KiB at a time, so one step's output stays near 4 MB. `read_all` still gathers up to its `max_size` (default 1 GiB): pass a smaller one for untrusted servers. Affected: 0.51.0 and earlier.
changelog: - Security (std/http client, native backends): a streaming client read of a gzip response gave the whole received chunk to the decoder at once, so about 1 MB of hostile gzip could ask for up to 1 GiB of output in one step (6.4 GB of memory in 0.51.0 for a 1000 MB bomb, now 23 MB); the body now goes to the decoder 4 KiB at a time, so one step's output stays near 4 MB. `read_all` still gathers up to its `max_size` (default 1 GiB): pass a smaller one for untrusted servers. Affected: 0.51.0 and earlier.
